question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in indirect speech.

 

The manager said, "I am reviewing the quarterly sales report."
option_1: The manager said that he was reviewing the quarterly sales report.
option_2: The manager said that he is reviewing the quarterly sales report.
option_3: The manager said that he had been reviewing the quarterly sales report.
option_4: The manager said that he reviews the quarterly sales report.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. The manager said that he was reviewing the quarterly sales report.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The present continuous ("am reviewing") in direct speech backshifts to the past continuous ("was reviewing") when reported with a past-tense reporting verb such as "said". The pronoun "I" also shifts to "he".

◦ Complete sentence: The manager said that he was reviewing the quarterly sales report.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2: "...is reviewing..." — the present continuous is wrongly left unchanged; it must backshift to "was reviewing".

 

• Option 3: "...had been reviewing..." — this is the past perfect continuous, used for an action continuing up to a past point, which does not match the original present continuous.

 

• Option 4: "...reviews..." — the simple present drops the continuous aspect of the original statement, which must be preserved.

 

NOTE

 

• She said, "I am cooking dinner." → she said that she was cooking dinner (present continuous → past continuous).

question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in indirect speech.

 

The coach said, "We will win the championship this year."
option_1: The coach said that they will win the championship this year.
option_2: The coach said that they would win the championship that year.
option_3: The coach said that they would win the championship this year.
option_4: The coach said that we would win the championship that year.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. The coach said that they would win the championship that year.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The future "will" in direct speech backshifts to "would", the pronoun "we" shifts to "they", and the time word "this year" shifts to "that year".

◦ Complete sentence: The coach said that they would win the championship that year.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: "...will win...this year." — "will" is wrongly left unchanged instead of backshifting to "would".

 

• Option 3: "...would win...this year." — the modal is correctly backshifted, but "this year" is wrongly left unchanged instead of "that year".

 

• Option 4: "...we would win...that year." — the pronoun "we" is wrongly retained instead of shifting to "they".

 

NOTE

 

• He said, "We will finish the project this month." → he said that they would finish the project that month (will → would, with pronoun and time-word shift).

question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in direct speech.

 

The clerk told the applicant that the form had been submitted successfully.
option_1: The clerk said to the applicant, "The form was submitted successfully."
option_2: The clerk told the applicant, "The form had been submitted successfully."
option_3: The clerk said to the applicant, "The form has been submitted successfully."
option_4: The clerk said to the applicant, "The form will have been submitted successfully."
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. The clerk said to the applicant, "The form has been submitted successfully.".

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The past perfect passive ("had been submitted") in indirect speech un-backshifts to the present perfect passive ("has been submitted") in direct speech.

◦ Complete sentence: The clerk said to the applicant, "The form has been submitted successfully."

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: "...was submitted successfully." — the simple past active drops the perfect and passive aspect of the original; it should be "has been submitted".

 

• Option 2: "...had been submitted successfully." — the past perfect is wrongly left unchanged in direct speech instead of being un-backshifted to the present perfect.

 

• Option 4: "...will have been submitted successfully." — the future perfect is an unwarranted tense shift that changes the meaning of the sentence.

 

NOTE

 

• She told him that the results had been declared. → she said to him, "The results have been declared." (past perfect → present perfect, in un-backshifting).

question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in indirect speech.

 

The trainer said to the athletes, "Warm up properly before the race."
option_1: The trainer said the athletes to warm up properly before the race.
option_2: The trainer advised the athletes warming up properly before the race.
option_3: The trainer advises the athletes to warm up properly before the race.
option_4: The trainer advised the athletes to warm up properly before the race.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. The trainer advised the athletes to warm up properly before the race.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• An imperative giving advice is reported using a suitable reporting verb such as "advised" followed by the object and the to-infinitive: "advised the athletes to warm up".

◦ Complete sentence: The trainer advised the athletes to warm up properly before the race.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: "said the athletes to warm up..." — "said" cannot directly take a personal object in this way; a verb like "advised" or "told" is required.

 

• Option 2: "...advised the athletes warming up..." — the gerund "warming" is wrongly used instead of the required to-infinitive "to warm up".

 

• Option 3: "...advises the athletes to warm up..." — the reporting verb is wrongly kept in the present tense instead of the past tense "advised".

 

NOTE

 

• The officer said to the recruits, "Report at six sharp." → the officer ordered the recruits to report at six sharp (imperative advice/order → reporting verb + object + to-infinitive).

question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in indirect speech.

 

The captain said to the team, "Let us practise for two extra hours today."
option_1: The captain suggested to the team that they should practise for two extra hours that day.
option_2: The captain ordered the team that let them practise for two extra hours that day.
option_3: The captain suggested to the team that they should practise for two extra hours today.
option_4: The captain told the team to practise for two extra hours that day.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. The captain suggested to the team that they should practise for two extra hours that day.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• A suggestion beginning with "Let us" is reported using "suggested that ... should", and the time word "today" shifts to "that day".

◦ Complete sentence: The captain suggested to the team that they should practise for two extra hours that day.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2: "ordered the team that let them practise..." — this ungrammatically mixes the reporting verb "ordered" with the imperative form "let them", which cannot occur inside a reported clause.

 

• Option 3: "...they should practise...today." — the modal "should" is correctly used, but the time word "today" is wrongly left unchanged instead of "that day".

 

• Option 4: "...told the team to practise..." — replacing the suggestion structure with "told...to" changes the sense from a suggestion to a command.

 

NOTE

 

• She said, "Let us donate blood this week." → she suggested that they should donate blood that week ("let us" + suggestion → "suggested that...should").

question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in indirect speech.

 

The interviewer asked the candidate, "Do you have any prior experience in this field?"
option_1: The interviewer asked the candidate that did he have any prior experience in that field.
option_2: The interviewer asked the candidate whether he had any prior experience in that field.
option_3: The interviewer asked the candidate if he has any prior experience in that field.
option_4: The interviewer asked the candidate whether he had any prior experience in this field.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. The interviewer asked the candidate whether he had any prior experience in that field.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• A yes/no question is reported using "whether/if" followed by statement word order (not the interrogative order), with the verb backshifted and "this" shifting to "that".

◦ Complete sentence: The interviewer asked the candidate whether he had any prior experience in that field.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: "...that did he have...that field." — "that" is the wrong connector for a yes/no question, and the interrogative order "did he have" is wrongly retained instead of "he had".

 

• Option 3: "...if he has...that field." — "if" is an acceptable connector, but "has" is wrongly left unchanged instead of backshifting to "had".

 

• Option 4: "...whether he had...this field." — the tense is correctly backshifted, but "this field" is wrongly left unchanged instead of "that field".

 

NOTE

 

• He asked, "Do you like this city?" → he asked whether I liked that city (yes/no question → whether/if + statement order).

question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in indirect speech.

 

The officer asked the driver, "Why did you not stop at the checkpoint?"
option_1: The officer asked the driver why he did not stop at the checkpoint.
option_2: The officer asked the driver why had he not stopped at the checkpoint.
option_3: The officer asked the driver why he had not stopped at the checkpoint.
option_4: The officer asked the driver that why he had not stopped at the checkpoint.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. The officer asked the driver why he had not stopped at the checkpoint.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• A wh-question is reported using the wh-word followed directly by statement word order, with the verb backshifted to the past perfect: "did not stop" becomes "had not stopped".

◦ Complete sentence: The officer asked the driver why he had not stopped at the checkpoint.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: "...why he did not stop..." — the simple past is wrongly left unchanged instead of backshifting to the past perfect "had not stopped".

 

• Option 2: "...why had he not stopped..." — the interrogative word order "had he" is wrongly retained instead of the statement order "he had".

 

• Option 4: "...that why he had not stopped..." — the superfluous connector "that" is wrongly added before the wh-word, which cannot be used with wh-questions.

 

NOTE

 

• She asked, "Why are you late?" → she asked why I was late (wh-question → wh-word + statement order, no "that").

question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in indirect speech.

 

She said, "What a magnificent painting this is!"
option_1: She exclaimed that what a magnificent painting it was.
option_2: She said that it was a magnificent painting.
option_3: She exclaimed that it is a magnificent painting.
option_4: She exclaimed that it was a magnificent painting.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. She exclaimed that it was a magnificent painting.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• An exclamatory sentence beginning with "What a...!" is reported using "exclaimed that", dropping the exclamatory structure and converting it into a plain statement, with the verb backshifted.

◦ Complete sentence: She exclaimed that it was a magnificent painting.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: "...that what a magnificent painting it was." — the exclamatory structure "what a" is wrongly retained inside the noun clause instead of being converted into a plain statement.

 

• Option 2: "She said that..." — the neutral reporting verb "said" is used instead of "exclaimed", losing the exclamatory force of the original sentence.

 

• Option 3: "...that it is a magnificent painting." — "is" is wrongly left unchanged instead of backshifting to "was".

 

NOTE

 

• He said, "What a lovely garden this is!" → he exclaimed that it was a lovely garden ("what a...!" → "exclaimed that" + plain statement).

question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in indirect speech.

 

The witness said, "I saw the accident near the traffic signal."
option_1: The witness said that he had seen the accident near the traffic signal.
option_2: The witness said that he saw the accident near the traffic signal.
option_3: The witness said that he has seen the accident near the traffic signal.
option_4: The witness said that he was seeing the accident near the traffic signal.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. The witness said that he had seen the accident near the traffic signal.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The simple past ("saw") in direct speech backshifts to the past perfect ("had seen") when reported with a past-tense reporting verb.

◦ Complete sentence: The witness said that he had seen the accident near the traffic signal.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2: "...he saw..." — the simple past is wrongly left unchanged instead of backshifting to the past perfect.

 

• Option 3: "...he has seen..." — the present perfect is wrongly used instead of the past perfect "had seen".

 

• Option 4: "...he was seeing..." — the past continuous wrongly changes the aspect of the original completed action.

 

NOTE

 

• He said, "I finished my homework." → he said that he had finished his homework (simple past → past perfect).

question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in indirect speech.

 

The doctor said to me, "You must complete the full course of antibiotics."
option_1: The doctor told me that I had to complete the full course of antibiotics.
option_2: The doctor told me that I must complete the full course of antibiotics.
option_3: The doctor told me that you must complete the full course of antibiotics.
option_4: The doctor said me that I must complete the full course of antibiotics.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. The doctor told me that I must complete the full course of antibiotics.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• When "must" expresses a necessary obligation or strong advice, it usually remains "must" in indirect speech, and the pronoun "you" shifts to "I" since the listener has become the reporter.

◦ Complete sentence: The doctor told me that I must complete the full course of antibiotics.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: "...I had to complete..." — "had to" wrongly replaces "must"; a standing necessity or strong obligation is usually retained as "must".

 

• Option 3: "...you must complete..." — the pronoun "you" is wrongly retained instead of shifting to "I".

 

• Option 4: "The doctor said me that..." — "said me" is an incorrect construction; it should be "told me" or "said to me".

 

NOTE

 

• She said to him, "You must attend the ceremony." → she told him that he must attend the ceremony ("must" of obligation retained; pronoun shift).

question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in direct speech.

 

The teacher said that she checked the attendance register every morning.
option_1: The teacher said, "I checked the attendance register every morning."
option_2: The teacher said, "She checks the attendance register every morning."
option_3: The teacher said, "I check the attendance register every morning."
option_4: The teacher says, "I check the attendance register every morning."
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. The teacher said, "I check the attendance register every morning.".

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• A habitual action reported in the simple past ("checked") un-backshifts to the simple present ("check") in direct speech, and the pronoun "she" shifts to "I".

◦ Complete sentence: The teacher said, "I check the attendance register every morning."

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: "I checked..." — the simple past is wrongly retained instead of un-backshifting to the simple present.

 

• Option 2: "She checks..." — the pronoun is wrongly left as "She" instead of shifting to the first person "I" inside the quotation.

 

• Option 4: "The teacher says..." — the reporting verb is wrongly changed to the present tense "says" instead of remaining "said".

 

NOTE

 

• He said that he played chess every evening. → he said, "I play chess every evening." (habitual simple past → simple present, in un-backshifting).

question:

The pilot informed the passengers that the aircraft was descending for landing.
option_1: The pilot said to the passengers, "The aircraft was descending for landing."
option_2: The pilot said to the passengers, "The aircraft had been descending for landing."
option_3: The pilot said to the passengers, "The aircraft has been descending for landing."
option_4: The pilot said to the passengers, "The aircraft is descending for landing."
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. The pilot said to the passengers, "The aircraft is descending for landing.".

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The past continuous ("was descending") in indirect speech un-backshifts to the present continuous ("is descending") in direct speech.

◦ Complete sentence: The pilot said to the passengers, "The aircraft is descending for landing."

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: "...was descending..." — the past continuous is wrongly left unchanged instead of un-backshifting to the present continuous.

 

• Option 2: "...had been descending..." — the past perfect continuous is an incorrect over-backshift that does not match the original tense.

question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in indirect speech.

 

The librarian said, "I can renew your membership for another year."
option_1: The librarian said that she could renew my membership for another year.
option_2: The librarian said that she can renew my membership for another year.
option_3: The librarian said that she could renew your membership for another year.
option_4: The librarian said that she could renew his membership for another year.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. The librarian said that she could renew my membership for another year.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The modal "can" backshifts to "could", and the pronoun "your" shifts to "my" since the person addressed is now the one reporting the speech.

◦ Complete sentence: The librarian said that she could renew my membership for another year.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2: "...she can renew..." — "can" is wrongly left unchanged instead of backshifting to "could".

 

• Option 3: "...could renew your membership..." — the pronoun "your" is wrongly retained instead of shifting to "my".

 

• Option 4: "...could renew his membership..." — the pronoun "his" is incorrect; it should shift to "my".

 

NOTE

 

• He said, "I can lend you my notes." → he said that he could lend me his notes (can → could; pronoun shift).

question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in indirect speech.

 

The tourist guide said, "This monument was built here nearly four hundred years ago."
option_1: The tourist guide said that this monument had been built here nearly four hundred years before.
option_2: The tourist guide said that that monument had been built there nearly four hundred years before.
option_3: The tourist guide said that that monument was built there nearly four hundred years ago.
option_4: The tourist guide said that this monument had been built there nearly four hundred years ago.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. The tourist guide said that that monument had been built there nearly four hundred years before.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In indirect speech, the demonstrative "this" shifts to "that", the place word "here" shifts to "there", the time word "ago" shifts to "before", and the simple past passive backshifts to the past perfect passive.

◦ Complete sentence: The tourist guide said that that monument had been built there nearly four hundred years before.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: "...this monument had been built here...before." — "this" and "here" are wrongly left unchanged instead of shifting to "that" and "there".

 

• Option 3: "...that monument was built there...ago." — the passive is wrongly left in the simple past instead of backshifting to "had been built", and "ago" is wrongly left unchanged instead of "before".

 

• Option 4: "...this monument had been built there...ago." — "here" is correctly shifted to "there", but "this" and "ago" are wrongly left unchanged.

 

NOTE

 

• She said, "I met him here yesterday." → she said that she had met him there the day before (here → there; yesterday → the day before).

question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in indirect speech.

 

The lifeguard shouted to the swimmers, "Don't swim beyond the flags!"
option_1: The lifeguard warned the swimmers to not swim beyond the flags.
option_2: The lifeguard warned the swimmers don't swim beyond the flags.
option_3: The lifeguard warned the swimmers not to swim beyond the flags.
option_4: The lifeguard warned the swimmers that not swim beyond the flags.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. The lifeguard warned the swimmers not to swim beyond the flags.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• A negative imperative is reported using a suitable reporting verb such as "warned" followed by the object and "not to" + base verb, with "not" placed before "to".

◦ Complete sentence: The lifeguard warned the swimmers not to swim beyond the flags.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: "...to not swim..." — the negation is misplaced; the standard form places "not" before "to": "not to swim".

 

• Option 2: "...warned the swimmers don't swim..." — the original imperative form "don't swim" is wrongly retained instead of being converted into the infinitive form.

 

• Option 4: "...that not swim..." — the use of "that" with a bare, unconjugated clause is ungrammatical.

 

NOTE

 

• The guard said, "Don't touch the wires!" → the guard warned them not to touch the wires (negative imperative → warned/told + object + not to + base verb).

◦ Complete sentence: The engineer said that he had been testing that machine since morning.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: "...he has been testing..." — the present perfect continuous is wrongly left unchanged instead of backshifting to the past perfect continuous.

 

• Option 2: "...had been testing this machine..." — the tense is correctly backshifted, but "this" is wrongly left unchanged instead of shifting to "that".

 

• Option 3: "...had tested that machine..." — the continuous aspect is wrongly dropped; it should remain "had been testing".

question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in indirect speech.

 

She said, "I am going to submit my resignation tomorrow."
option_1: She said that she was going to submit her resignation the next day.
option_2: She said that she was going to submit her resignation tomorrow.
option_3: She said that she is going to submit her resignation the next day.
option_4: She said that she would submit her resignation the next day.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. She said that she was going to submit her resignation the next day.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Am/is/are going to" expressing a planned intention backshifts to "was/were going to", and the time word "tomorrow" shifts to "the next day".

◦ Complete sentence: She said that she was going to submit her resignation the next day.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2: "...was going to submit...tomorrow." — the tense is correctly backshifted, but "tomorrow" is wrongly left unchanged instead of shifting to "the next day".

 

• Option 3: "...is going to submit...the next day." — "is going to" is wrongly left unchanged instead of backshifting to "was going to".

 

• Option 4: "...would submit...the next day." — replacing "was going to" with "would" changes the planned-intention nuance of the original sentence.

 

NOTE

 

• He said, "I am going to buy a new car next month." → he said that he was going to buy a new car the following month (am going to → was going to; next month → the following month).

question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in direct speech.

 

The customer asked the shopkeeper whether the warranty could be extended by a year.
option_1: The customer said to the shopkeeper, "Could the warranty be extended by a year?"
option_2: The customer said to the shopkeeper, "Can the warranty be extended by a year?"
option_3: The customer asked to the shopkeeper, "Can the warranty be extended by a year?"
option_4: The customer said to the shopkeeper, "Whether the warranty can be extended by a year?"
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. The customer said to the shopkeeper, "Can the warranty be extended by a year?".

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The modal "could" in indirect speech un-backshifts to "can" in direct speech, and the connector "whether" is dropped, restoring the interrogative word order.

◦ Complete sentence: The customer said to the shopkeeper, "Can the warranty be extended by a year?"

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: "Could the warranty..." — "could" is wrongly left unchanged instead of un-backshifting to "can".

 

• Option 3: "The customer asked to the shopkeeper..." — "asked" does not take "to" before the person addressed; it should be "asked the shopkeeper" or "said to the shopkeeper".

 

• Option 4: "Whether the warranty can be extended...?" — the reported-speech connector "whether" cannot appear inside a direct quotation.

 

NOTE

 

• He asked me if he might borrow my pen. → he said to me, "May I borrow your pen?" (connector dropped and interrogative order restored, in un-backshifting).

question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in indirect speech.

 

He said, "How swiftly the river flows after the monsoon!"
option_1: He exclaimed how swiftly the river flowed after the monsoon.
option_2: He said that the river flowed swiftly after the monsoon.
option_3: He exclaimed that the river flowed swiftly after the monsoon.
option_4: He exclaimed that the river flows swiftly after the monsoon.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. He exclaimed that the river flowed swiftly after the monsoon.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• An exclamatory sentence beginning with "How...!" is reported using "exclaimed that", dropping the exclamatory structure and backshifting the verb.

◦ Complete sentence: He exclaimed that the river flowed swiftly after the monsoon.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: "He exclaimed how swiftly..." — the exclamatory structure "how" is wrongly retained inside the noun clause instead of being converted into a plain statement introduced by "that".

 

• Option 2: "He said that..." — the neutral reporting verb "said" is used instead of "exclaimed", losing the exclamatory force.

 

• Option 4: "...that the river flows..." — "flows" is wrongly left unchanged instead of backshifting to "flowed".

 

NOTE

 

• She said, "How quickly the children have grown!" → she exclaimed that the children had grown quickly ("how...!" → "exclaimed that" + plain statement).

question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in direct speech.

 

The senior members suggested to the club that they should organise a blood donation camp that month.
option_1: The senior members said to the club, "Let us organise a blood donation camp that month."
option_2: The senior members said to the club, "Let we organise a blood donation camp this month."

option_4: The senior members said to the club, "Let us organise a blood donation camp this month."
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. The senior members said to the club, "Let us organise a blood donation camp this month.".

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Suggested that...should" un-backshifts to the original "Let us" form, and the time word "that month" shifts back to "this month".

◦ Complete sentence: The senior members said to the club, "Let us organise a blood donation camp this month."

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: "...Let us organise...that month." — "that month" is wrongly retained instead of shifting back to "this month" in direct speech.

 

• Option 2: "...Let we organise...this month." — "let we" is an incorrect pronoun form; the fixed idiom is "let us".

 

• Option 3: "...We should organise...this month." — replacing "let us" with a plain modal statement does not reconstruct the original suggestion structure.

 

NOTE

 

• They suggested that they should plant more trees that year. → they said, "Let us plant more trees this year." ("suggested that...should" → "let us", in un-backshifting).

question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in direct speech.

 

The journalist asked the minister why the project had been delayed for two years.
option_1: The journalist said to the minister, "Why has the project been delayed for two years?"
option_2: The journalist said to the minister, "Why had the project been delayed for two years?"
option_3: The journalist asked to the minister, "Why has the project been delayed for two years?"
option_4: The journalist said to the minister, "Why the project has been delayed for two years?"
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. The journalist said to the minister, "Why has the project been delayed for two years?".

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The past perfect passive ("had been delayed") un-backshifts to the present perfect passive ("has been delayed"), and the interrogative word order is restored with the auxiliary before the subject.

◦ Complete sentence: The journalist said to the minister, "Why has the project been delayed for two years?"

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2: "...Why had the project been delayed...?" — "had" is wrongly left unchanged instead of un-backshifting to "has".

 

• Option 3: "The journalist asked to the minister..." — "asked" does not take "to" before the person addressed.

 

• Option 4: "Why the project has been delayed...?" — the word order is wrong; the auxiliary "has" must come before the subject "the project" in a direct question.

 

NOTE

 

• She asked him why he had left early. → she said to him, "Why did you leave early?" (interrogative word order restored, in un-backshifting).

question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in indirect speech.

 

She asked, "Shall I close the window?"
option_1: She asked whether she shall close the window.
option_2: She asked whether she should close the window.
option_3: She asked if she would close the window.
option_4: She asked that should she close the window.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. She asked whether she should close the window.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Shall I...?" used to make an offer or suggestion is reported using "should", not "would", with the connector "whether/if" and statement word order.

◦ Complete sentence: She asked whether she should close the window.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: "...whether she shall close..." — "shall" is wrongly left unchanged instead of shifting to "should".

 

• Option 3: "...if she would close..." — "would" is the wrong modal here; an offer-type "Shall I...?" question shifts to "should", not "would".

 

• Option 4: "...that should she close..." — the connector "that" is wrong for a yes/no question, and the inverted order "should she" is wrongly retained instead of "she should".

 

NOTE

 

• He asked, "Shall we begin the meeting?" → he asked whether they should begin the meeting ("Shall I/we...?" offer → should).

question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in indirect speech.

 

He said, "It may rain heavily this evening."
option_1: He said that it may rain heavily that evening.
option_2: He said that it might rain heavily this evening.
option_3: He said that it might rain heavily that evening.
option_4: He said that it could rain heavily that evening.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. He said that it might rain heavily that evening.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The modal "may" backshifts to "might", and the time word "this evening" shifts to "that evening".

◦ Complete sentence: He said that it might rain heavily that evening.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: "...it may rain...that evening." — "may" is wrongly left unchanged instead of backshifting to "might".

 

• Option 2: "...it might rain...this evening." — the modal is correctly backshifted, but "this evening" is wrongly left unchanged instead of "that evening".

 

• Option 4: "...it could rain...that evening." — "could" wrongly substitutes for "might", changing the modal of possibility being tested.

 

NOTE

 

• She said, "It may snow tonight." → she said that it might snow that night (may → might; time-word shift).

question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in indirect speech.

 

The passenger said to the conductor, "Please stop the bus at the next junction."
option_1: The passenger requested the conductor that stop the bus at the next junction.
option_2: The passenger requested to the conductor to stop the bus at the next junction.
option_3: The passenger requested the conductor stopping the bus at the next junction.
option_4: The passenger requested the conductor to stop the bus at the next junction.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. The passenger requested the conductor to stop the bus at the next junction.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• A polite request beginning with "Please" is reported using "requested" followed by the object and the to-infinitive, without an additional preposition after "requested".

◦ Complete sentence: The passenger requested the conductor to stop the bus at the next junction.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: "...requested the conductor that stop..." — the ungrammatical use of "that" followed by a bare verb instead of the to-infinitive.

 

• Option 2: "...requested to the conductor to stop..." — the extra preposition "to" after "requested" is unnecessary and incorrect; "requested" takes a direct object.

 

• Option 3: "...requested the conductor stopping..." — the gerund "stopping" is wrongly used instead of the required to-infinitive "to stop".

 

NOTE

 

• She said to him, "Please lend me your umbrella." → she requested him to lend her his umbrella (polite request → requested + object + to-infinitive).

question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in indirect speech.

 

The captain told his crew, "We must repair our ship before the storm reaches us."
option_1: The captain told his crew that they must repair their ship before the storm reached them.
option_2: The captain told his crew that they must repair their ship before the storm reaches them.
option_3: The captain told his crew that we must repair our ship before the storm reached us.
option_4: The captain told his crew that they must repair their ship before the storm had reached them.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. The captain told his crew that they must repair their ship before the storm reached them.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The pronouns "we/our/us" shift to "they/their/them" since the crew addressed are third parties to the reporter, and the simple present "reaches" in the subordinate time clause backshifts to the simple past "reached".

◦ Complete sentence: The captain told his crew that they must repair their ship before the storm reached them.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2: "...before the storm reaches them." — "reaches" is wrongly left unchanged instead of backshifting to "reached".

 

• Option 3: "...we must repair our ship before the storm reached us." — the pronouns "we/our/us" are wrongly retained instead of shifting to "they/their/them".

 

• Option 4: "...before the storm had reached them." — the past perfect is an unwarranted over-backshift; both actions are sequential simple-past events joined by "before".

 

NOTE

 

• They said, "We will leave before the guests arrive." → they said that they would leave before the guests arrived (pronoun shift; subordinate clause verb backshifts to simple past).
